Signs of the World

International symbol of access

History

In 1968, Rehabilitation International's president Norman Acton asked Karl Montan, chairman of its technology and accessibility commission, to develop a symbol for accessible facilities. Danish design student Susanne Koefoed drew a figure in a wheelchair, influenced by Scandinavian design. With a round head added, it was approved at the group's 1969 World Congress in Dublin, then gained prominence through signs made by 3M and became part of ISO 7001.

Adoption

A United Nations experts' meeting formally accepted the symbol in 1974. New York and Connecticut use a newer version that shows the figure leaning forward in motion.
